articles.title: Rapido’s Manasvi Mann Gets Representation On National Gig Workers' Welfare Panel
articles.description: The Government of India has constituted the National Social Security Board for gig and platform workers, bringing together representatives from digital platforms, worker organisations, government bodies and policy experts to discuss social protection measures for the country's growing gig workforce. The constitution of the Board was formally announced through an Extraordinary Gazette notification by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Manasvi Mann, General Counsel and Head of Corporate Affairs and Public Policy at Rapido, has been nominated as a member. Rapido is the only app-based passenger mobility aggregator among the five platform companies selected for representation. Manasvi Mann to Represent Rapido on National Board The Board comprises representatives from digital platforms, worker organisations, central and state governments, and subject-matter experts. It will contribute to the development and implementation of social security and welfare measures for gig and platform workers. Mann's nomination gives Rapido an opportunity to represent the app-based passenger mobility sector in discussions on worker welfare and social protection, alongside other industry and government representatives. Focus on Welfare of Platform-Based Workers Platform-based services have become an important source of livelihood across India. In the passenger mobility segment, bike-taxi, auto and cab services provide earning opportunities to individuals while raising specific considerations around financial security and access to welfare benefits. The Board will address the broader requirements of workers engaged in these services and other segments of the platform economy. Industry Participation in Gig Economy Discussions Rapido's inclusion provides an opportunity for the passenger mobility sector to bring its operational experience and industry perspective into national-level discussions. The participation of platform companies alongside worker organisations and government representatives is intended to ensure that different stakeholder perspectives are considered while developing social protection measures. As gig and platform-based employment continues to expand, access to welfare benefits and financial security remains an important consideration for workers across the sector.

articles.title: Nita Ambani Anant Ashray: Reliance Foundation Unveils 100-Acre Township In Karjat
articles.description: Mumbai, November 1, 2026: Reliance Foundation has announced plans to establish a 100-acre township in Karjat, near Mumbai, to provide lifelong residential care to more than 5,000 people, including orphaned children, senior citizens and persons with developmental disabilities. Named Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, the not-for-profit initiative was announced by Reliance Foundation Founder and Chairperson Nita M. Ambani, who performed the Bhumi Pujan and groundbreaking ceremony on Sunday. The project will be developed in phases, subject to necessary approvals. The township is expected to support a community of around 15,000 people, including residents, caregivers, healthcare professionals and support staff. It will combine residential accommodation with specialised medical care, rehabilitation, education and vocational training. Nita Ambani Announces Long-Term Care Initiative Speaking at the ceremony, Nita Ambani said the project aims to provide a secure home and access to healthcare and development opportunities for people requiring long-term support. “For me and my family, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray is a beginning very close to our hearts. It is a step towards building a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort. We envision a community where compassionate care and medical support come together with the warmth of family life, where people live surrounded by nature, with opportunities to learn, work, make friends, and experience the joy of festivals and celebrations.” She added, “As a mother, my deepest hope is that parents who have spent a lifetime worrying about who will care for their children when they are no longer there can find peace in knowing that their child will always have a home and a family of their own. Above all, we hope Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray gives every person, at every age, the chance to live with dignity and look forward to each new day with hope,” Township to Have Eight Residential Villages The proposed development will comprise eight residential villages named after Indian rivers. Each village will have distinct colours, symbols and sensory gardens to help residents navigate their surroundings. Residents will live in family-style homes with dedicated caregivers and house parents. Individual care plans will cover healthcare, education, skill development, employment and personal well-being, with reviews at least every six months. The campus will also include a hospital, temple, playgrounds, gardens, farms, workshops and cafés. Specialised Healthcare and Rehabilitation Facilities A dedicated hospital will provide developmental medicine, epilepsy care, special-needs dentistry and palliative care. Rehabilitation services will include physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and hydrotherapy. Other proposed facilities include inclusive sports and recreational spaces, special education services, a mainstream school for staff members' children and an animal companionship farm developed with expertise from Vantara. The township will also have a bakery, café and craft studios to provide vocational training and employment opportunities. Family respite homes, mobile medical clinics, a hospice wing and a national training academy for disability-care professionals are also part of the plan. Services to Extend to Nearby Communities The project will extend selected services to neighbouring villages and districts. Around 1,000 people from the region are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities. Outreach programmes, respite care and community healthcare services are also planned. The initiative will focus on people with developmental disabilities, cerebral palsy, autism, epilepsy and complex medical conditions who require specialised and continuous care. It also aims to support families who have limited access to long-term residential care and rehabilitation facilities. Reliance Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Reliance Industries Limited, works across healthcare, education, rural transformation, sports, disaster management, women's empowerment, urban renewal, and arts and culture. The foundation says its programmes have reached more than 100 million people across over 98,000 villages and urban locations in India. The Karjat project will expand its work in social welfare, with a focus on lifelong care and support for vulnerable individuals.
